bib.title: GDPO: Group reward-Decoupled Normalization Policy Optimization for Multi-reward RL Optimization

question: Is GRPO suitable for multi-reward RL, and if not, what normalisation preserves the differences between reward combinations?
hypothesis: Summing rewards before group normalisation collapses distinct reward combinations into identical advantages; normalising each reward separately restores resolution and improves convergence.
contributions: Analysis of GRPO reward collapse in multi-reward RL
GDPO: group-wise decoupled normalisation of each reward, then batch-wise advantage normalisation
A systematic overview of reward weighting and conditioned reward functions for priority variation
Experiments on tool calling, math reasoning and coding reasoning showing GDPO beats GRPO

method.summary: GDPO normalises each reward separately within the rollout group (Eq. 4), sums the per-reward advantages (Eq. 5, optionally weighted, Eq. 7), then normalises that sum over the batch (Eq. 6). Compared with GRPO on summed reward in verl across tool calling (2 rewards), math (2 rewards) and coding (2 and 3 rewards).
method.task: multi-reward RL fine-tuning of LLMs (policy optimisation)

datasets.name: Eurus-2-RL (coding)
datasets.size: 24k coding problems with multiple test cases

datasets.name: PRIME validation set: Apps, CodeContests, Codeforces, Taco

training.objective: GRPO/GDPO clipped policy-gradient (Eq. 3) with decoupled per-reward advantages (Eq. 4-6); KL term used (kl_coef 0.001 tool, kl_loss_coef 0.0005 math/code)
training.seeds: 5 runs for tool calling (median + IQR curves); runs for math and coding not stated

other.weights: w_correct=1, w_length in {0.25,0.5,0.75,1.0} in priority study

inference.prompting: DeepSeek-R1 prompt format for math; ToolRL system prompt for tool calling (Appendix B)
